P fr. 2 uses the same names. Xylander's correction classicises the author's terminology, which the principles forbid. Edition 1 also has to move Xylander's dagger from δὶς διὰ πασῶν to δὶς διὰ πέντε by its own judgement. After reading the notes: edition 1 says the sense is octave + fourth, which is true, but this does not justify changing a unanimous, deliberately introduced term. Edition 2's argument agrees with mine. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων … δὶς διὰ πέντε Bas. H Par. V (cf. 28.6–7 and P fr. 2) : διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων … διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ πέντε Xyl. in marg. Note that Xylander's dagger stands before δὶς διὰ πασῶν (28.12), but by sense the note belongs to δὶς διὰ πέντε. A translation note should say that the author's 'double fourth/fifth' means the fourth/fifth above the octave (8:3, 3:1).

verdicts.reasoning: There are two elements. (1) βαρεῖ / βάρει: V has βαρεῖ. Bas. has βαρεί, a misprint whose accent stands on the ultima, so it agrees with V on the word. H (βά|ρει, divided at the line end) and Par. have βάρει. Sense requires the substantivised adjective: τοῦ ὀξέος τῷ βαρεῖ, 'the high note with the low'. The author pairs the two adjectives in the next lines, τῶν βαρέων τοῖς ὀξέσιν, ἢ τῶν ὀξέων τοῖς βαρέσι (28.23–24, unanimous), and again at 30.2 (τοῦ βαρέος πρὸς τὸ ὀξύτερον). βάρος ('weight') is not used for pitch: the noun for lowness of pitch is βαρύτης. H's accent is a common misplacement in Byzantine accentuation, and the collator's own note reads H's βά|ρει as = βαρεῖ. (2) ὀξέως / ὀξέος: all witnesses have ὀξέως, but with the article τοῦ it can only be the genitive. The author's own genitive of this declension is βαρέος (30.2, Bas. H Par. V), so ὀξέως looks like a scribal ο/ω spelling assimilated to the common adverb. I treat it as orthography to be normalised, not as the author's morphology. After reading the notes: edition 2 argues βαρεῖ on the same grounds. Edition 1 has no note and simply follows H Par. Not revised. If the project prefers to keep ὀξέως as a Byzantine genitive, print τοῦ ὀξέως τῷ βαρεῖ; the substantive decision is βαρεῖ.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: βαρεῖ V (βαρεί Bas.) : βάρει H Par. Orthographica (or apparatus, since the form borders on morphology): ὀξέος scripsi : ὀξέως Bas. H Par. V.

verdicts.reasoning: προσωνυμίας is unanimous: Bas. 29.5, H 67r.17, Par. 24r.21, V 79r.21–79v.1 (προσωνυ-|μίας). No witness and no marginal note has προσηγορίας, and edition 2 gives no note for its reading. It looks like a slip, contaminated by τὰς τοιάσδε προσηγορίας at 27.22. προσωνυμίας οὐκ ἔτυχε ('received no name', of the remainder of the fourth smaller than a diesis) is good Greek and fits the author's φερωνυμίας (28.5). After reading the notes: edition 1's only note at this place concerns another passage (Bas. 25.4) and is irrelevant here. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: No entry needed: προσωνυμίας is unanimous and προσηγορίας has no witness. At most an internal note that edition 2's προσηγορίας was a slip.

verdicts.reasoning: All witnesses have δὶς at both places: Bas. 29.8–9 (with Xylander's asterisks), H 67r.20–21, Par. 24v.2–3 and V 79v.4–6. The deletion rests only on Xylander's margin ('abundant omnino, et delenda sunt'), so it is a conjecture. The expression continues the author's terminology of 28.6 and 28.11, where 'δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων' is the fourth a second time, above the octave. The figures fix the meaning: δι’ ὀκτὼ καὶ ἡμιτονίου (8½ tones = 6 + 2½) and δι’ ἐννέα καὶ ἡμιτονίου (9½ = 6 + 3½). So δὶς is not a multiplier: a literal octave + double fourth would be 11 tones. The phrase means 'the octave and the fourth again'. The same wording recurs at 29.14–15 in H V and partly in Par. It therefore stands in the archetype at four places, already in H (1040), which makes a repeated accident unlikely. After reading the notes: edition 1's reason ('redundant doubling') is a classicising argument. Edition 2's account agrees with mine. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: δὶς (bis) Bas. H Par. V : del. Xyl. in marg. ('abundant omnino, et delenda sunt'). A translation note should say that 8½ and 9½ tones = octave + fourth and octave + fifth.

verdicts.reasoning: There are two elements. (1) δὲ before διὰ πασῶν: only Bas. has it. H 67v.4, Par. 24v.8 and V 79v.11 have τοῦ διὰ πασῶν, and no witness, Bas. included, has δὲ before the next item (29.15). Bas. alone against H Par. V, so delete it. (2) δὶς: H (67v.4, 67v.6) and V (79v.11, 79v.13) have it twice. Par. lacks it in the first item but has it in the second (24v.10 καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε). Bas. lacks it in both, probably Xylander silently applying his own deletion from 29.8–9, where Bas. still prints δὶς with asterisks. So the archetype, including Par.'s branch, had δὶς here, as at 29.8–9 (unanimous). Par.'s single omission is an isolated slip or normalisation. The ratios (διπλασιεπιμερής = 8:3 = 16:6; τριπλάσιος = 3:1 = 18:6) confirm octave + fourth and octave + fifth, in the author's naming. Medium rather than high confidence because Par. agrees with Bas. in the first item. After reading the notes: edition 2's analysis matches mine. Edition 1 simply prints Bas. without argument. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: τοῦ διὰ πασῶν H Par. V : τοῦ δὲ διὰ πασῶν Bas. Then καὶ δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων H V : καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων Bas. Par. Then καὶ δὶς διὰ πέντε H Par. V : καὶ διὰ πέντε Bas. (cf. Xyl. ad 29.8–9).

verdicts.reasoning: P as reported (Vinc. 340.9–10, printed προ-|λαμβανόμενον with no footnote) reads προλαμβανόμενον. Inside ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩, P is the only witness, and a conjecture is allowed only when it gives no acceptable text. Here it does: 'the note taken first', i.e. the base term (cf. ἀπὸ τοῦ πρώτου φθόγγου, 27.19; κείσθω πρῶτος ἐν ἀριθμοῖς ὅρος, 29.17). It stands in a clear antithesis to the ἄμεσα, which are referred πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ αὐτῶν ἐγγὺς φθόγγους. Later in the fragment the ἔμμεσα are again compared πρὸς τοὺς ἄκρους … τῶν φθόγγων. Vincent was a specialist in Greek music, and he footnoted his corrections elsewhere in the fragment, yet he printed this form without comment. The referent is the same either way: note 1 of the fifteen counted in 28.19–22, i.e. the number 6 of the example. So nothing in the sense requires the change. After reading the notes: edition 2's case for προσλαμβανόμενον is strong. It is the technical name in exactly the same participial shape; the loss of a σ is trivial, possibly at Vincent's line break; and edition 2 reports the term at 25.4–5, which I could not check from my evidence. That case is strong enough for the apparatus but does not meet the rule for printing a conjecture. The P passage may also not be by the author, so the author's usage at 25.4–5 binds it less. Kept, with medium confidence.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: προλαμβανόμενον P (Vinc., without a note, divided προ-|λαμβανόμενον) : προσλαμβανόμενον fort. recte coni. (the technical name of note 1; cf. 25.4–5 if confirmed there). A translation note may name the proslambanomenos.

verdicts.reasoning: Vincent prints πεποίηνται (340.13) without a footnote, so this is P as reported. Edition 2's πεποίηται is neither P nor Vincent. The plural verb with a neuter plural subject (τὰ δὲ ἄμεσα … πεποίηνται) is the author's own construction in this same sentence: τὰ μὲν οὖν ἔμμεσα διαστήματα … ἔχουσι τὴν ἀναφοράν, and later τὰ … διαστήματα … κίρνανται. Making it singular would be classicising, against the principles. After reading the notes: edition 2 gives no note justifying the change. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: No apparatus entry is needed (P's reading is printed). If one is wanted: πεποίηνται P (Vinc.) : πεποίηται perperam edition 2 (not to be recorded as a variant).

verdicts.reasoning: P has ἐξυφθάρσεως at both places (Vinc. 340 n. 2, applied to 340.13–14 and 340.18). It is not a word, so P gives no acceptable text and a conjecture is permitted. Vincent's ἐξ φθάρσεως is itself a conjecture, and a bad one: ἐξ cannot stand before φ, and 'from destruction' does not fit κίρνανται / εἰς ἓν διάστημα. ἐκ συμφθάρσεως keeps every transmitted letter of -υφθάρσεως. It needs only the phonetic spelling ἐξ- for ἐκ σ- (κσ = ξ) and the loss of μ before φ. It is also the author's own phrase for exactly these 'incomposite' intervals formed as one: ὡς ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (27.10; H 66r.12–13 συμφθάρ|σεως), ἓν ἐκ συμφθάρσεως διάστημα (32.10–11) and ἓν διτόνιον ἐκ συμφθάρσεως (32.17), all unanimous. The fragment lists the same intervals as 27.6–7 (τριδίεσις, τριημιτόνιον, διτόνιον, τριτόνιον). After reading the notes: edition 1 makes the same arguments in fuller form. I agree.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus, at both places: ἐκ συμφθάρσεως coni. (cf. 27.10, 32.10–11, 32.17) : ἐξυφθάρσεως P (Vinc. n. 2) : ἐξ φθάρσεως Vinc. A cautious alternative for the text would be †ἐξυφθάρσεως†.

verdicts.reasoning: Vinc. 340 n. 4 reports 'Ms. κεκρυμμένων'. Vincent's κεκραμένων is a conjecture. P's reading gives good sense, so it must be kept: τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς κεκρυμμένων διαστημάτων means 'the intervals hidden, latent, in them' (in the tridiesis, trihemitone, ditone, tritone). This is exactly the doctrine of the main text: such an interval is δύναμιν μὲν ἔχον διαφόρων διαστημάτων, δι’ ἑνὸς δὲ διαστήματος ἀπηχούμενον (27.12–14). In the genitive absolute, the component intervals were assigned their ratios beforehand and lie hidden in the single interval, which then sounds as one. Vincent's form was prompted by κίρνανται at the end of the sentence. The author's συγκεκραμένον (32.12) lends it some colour, but that same echo makes κεκραμένων the easier reading, and a scribe would more likely have produced it than κεκρυμμένων. After reading the notes: edition 2 argues the same. Edition 1 has no note. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: κεκρυμμένων P : κεκραμένων Vinc. (cf. κίρνανται and 32.12 συγκεκραμένον).

verdicts.reasoning: P as reported reads ὅτι … τοῦτο (Vinc. 342 nn. 2–3: 'Ms. ὅτι', 'Ms. τοῦτο'). Vincent's ὅ, τι … οὔ πω is a double conjecture. P's text is sound: μονάδων μὴ τεμνομένων, ὅτι μηδὲ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς τοῦτο δέδοκται, 'the units not being cut, since not even the arithmeticians accept this', i.e. the division of the unit, which is indivisible in arithmetic. μηδέ in a causal clause is ordinary Byzantine usage. Vincent's change is needed only if ὅτι is taken as a relative, and it produces an awkward double negative (μηδὲ … οὔ πω). μονάδων (Vincent, for P's μονάδος) is common to both editions and is needed for agreement with τεμνομένων. After reading the notes: edition 1 makes the same argument. Edition 2 has no note. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: ὅτι … τοῦτο P : ὅ, τι … οὔ πω Vinc. Separately: μονάδων Vinc. : μονάδος P.

verdicts.reasoning: H 69r.19 has γοερώτερο(ν). Bas., Par. 26v.11 and V 82r.1 have γοέτερον. γοέτερον is no Greek form: there is no positive from which it could be formed. It is not Byzantine usage but a mechanical loss of the syllable -ρω- (γοε[ρώ]τερον), perhaps helped by the familiar ending -έτερος. The comparative of γοερός (short syllable before the ending) is regularly γοερώτερος. This is the case where the oldest manuscript corrects the shared error of the printed tradition and its relative V. It is also paired with παθητικώτερον, as the sense requires. Xylander's version ('ad … luctum ciendum efficacius') presupposes the comparative of γοερός. After reading the notes: edition 2 doubts the change in order not to 'classicise the author's possible usage', but an impossible form is not usage. Not convinced; no revision.
verdicts.apparatus: Apparatus: γοερώτερον H : γοέτερον Bas. Par. V.

verdicts.reasoning: παιήων is unanimous: Bas. 33.12, H 69v.20 (the collator confirms παιήων), Par. 27r.16 and V 82v.7. It is a genuine Greek form for the paean song (the Ionic-epic form, used in later literary Greek as well). It belongs to the author's diction, so changing it to παιών is a change of form, not an orthographic normalisation, and has no witness. After reading the notes: edition 2 gives no justification. Edition 1's notes concern ὑμέναιος, which both editions print. No revision.
verdicts.apparatus: No apparatus entry is needed (unanimous). Bas.'s ὑμεραῖος in the same line is recorded separately: ὑμέναιος H Par. V : ὑμεραῖος Bas. (misprint).

result.summary:
Judge B decided 12 places, first from the witnesses, then checked against both editions' notes. No initial decision was changed after the notes, though at P2-proslamb the conjecture προσλαμβανόμενον goes into the apparatus as a strong alternative.

Decisions:
- 28.11, 29.8, 29.14: the author's own naming is kept, against Xylander's classicising corrections. All witnesses have δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων / δὶς διὰ πέντε. The author introduces the name at 28.6–7, and the examples at 28.19–22 (11th note with 4th, 12th with 5th) and the tone counts at 29.8–10 (8½ and 9½ tones) show it means the fourth/fifth again above the octave. At 29.14 the H V text without δὲ is printed: δὲ is in Bas. alone, and Par. has δὶς in the second item.
- 28.18: τοῦ ὀξέος τῷ βαρεῖ is printed. βαρεῖ is the decisive point, read in V and, by accent position, in Bas.; ὀξέως is normalised to the author's own βαρέος type (30.2).
- 29.5: προσωνυμίας is unanimous; edition 2's προσηγορίας has no witness.
- 32.15: γοερώτερον (H) against the impossible γοέτερον of Bas. Par. V.
- 33.12: παιήων is unanimous.
- In the P fragment 2 (P-only passage, ⟨⟨ ⟩⟩), P as reported is printed wherever it gives sense: προλαμβανόμενον (medium confidence), πεποίηνται, κεκρυμμένων, ὅτι … τοῦτο. The one conjecture is ἐκ συμφθάρσεως for P's non-word ἐξυφθάρσεως; it is the author's own phrase at 27.10, 32.10–11 and 32.17.
